Reformat-only rewrite of getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory in CredentialHelper adds unrelated whitespace churn that inflates the diff
configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes takes a delay parameter and wires a 'delayed-authenticator' execution, but the only caller passes 0 — dead speculative generality

Provider id hardcoded as string literal 'keycloak-recovery-authn-codes' in CredentialHelper instead of referencing RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID, creating two spellings of the provider id that can silently drift

Optional-returning helper RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential's only new caller calls .get() unconditionally, causing raw NoSuchElementException (HTTP 500) in bean construction when no credential exists
Test config alias typo 'delayed-suthenticator-config' in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:133
Recovery codes stored as plaintext instead of SHA-512 hashes for federated users, dropping the security contract
Two incompatible on-disk formats for the same credential type, diverging between local and federated paths
Credential lookup order changed from local-only to federated-first, orphaning/shadowing existing local credentials without a migration or precedence rule
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage modified, destroying its purpose of testing unmodified legacy providers; a separate provider should have been created
Hardcoded provider id string 'keycloak-recovery-authn-codes' replaces the PROVIDER_ID constant, risking silent null and NPE if the id changes
Error semantics changed to a bare RuntimeException with no message, thrown after codes are displayed but before persistence, leaving the required action pending and codes invalid
Plaintext recovery codes handed to user-storage providers via updateCredential and stored/compared unhashed, defeating 2FA for federated users
Recovery codes in user-storage path are replayable: no single-use consumption, isValid never marks codes as used
RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean constructor calls Optional.get() without presence check, causing NoSuchElementException/500 error on login page

The else branch of createRecoveryCodesCredential (local-storage fallback via recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential) is never exercised by any test in the diff; only the user-storage-created branch is tested

The IOException to RuntimeException branch in createRecoveryCodesCredential is unreachable dead code since JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString on a List<String> won't throw, and the RuntimeException wrap has no error context
The test adds a delayed-authenticator execution with delay=0 that is dead scaffolding — nothing tests or depends on the delay, adding an untested moving part to the flow under test

The test never verifies recovery code consumption/invalidation — no assertion that a used code fails on second login or that getCredential's federated-first lookup returns updated credentials, so code replay regressions would pass

The enterRecoveryCodes helper conflates 1-based code numbers with 0-based list indices — passing an int directly as a list index risks an off-by-one entering the wrong recovery code, masking a potential numbering bug

createRecoveryCodesCredential discards the hashed credentialModel and writes unhashed recovery codes in an incompatible format (bare JSON array) for user-storage users, causing parsing failures and lockout when the credential is read back
No cleanup of pre-existing local recovery-codes credential when regeneration lands in user storage, leaving a stale shadow credential that can silently reactivate if the federation is removed

getCredential precedence change silently shadows an existing local recovery-codes credential with any federated credential of the same type, with no backfill or reconciliation before the read path switches

Test provider updateCredential overwrites the recovery-codes field without round-trip of consumed-code state, and isValid compares against the full stored list without removing used codes, so codes are never marked used

Federated user credentialData stored as raw JSON array of code strings causes RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel to throw a parsing exception (500 error) during login validation
credentialModelOpt.get() is called without an isPresent() guard in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean, causing NoSuchElementException and a 500 error when no recovery-codes credential exists
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials silently swallows IOException and omits the recovery-codes credential from the returned stream, causing inconsistency with isConfiguredFor
Single-use semantics are lost for user-storage users: no code consumes/marks a used recovery code in the federated path, allowing indefinite replay of the same recovery code

session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes") result is never null-checked before calling .createCredential, causing NPE when the RECOVERY_CODES feature is disabled; also the provider id constant was replaced with duplicated hand-typed string literals

users.get(translateUserName(user.getUsername())) in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential dereferences the map result without a null check, causing NPE for users absent from the map instead of the local-storage fallback

goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage are never consumed after use — isValid never removes the matched code, breaking single-use contract for federated users

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the new recovery-codes branch deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, but it never removes the matched code from `myUser.recoveryCodes` (nor persists an updated list). This means a recovery code can be reused indefinitely for federated users backed by this storage implementation, violating the intended single-use behavior for recovery codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded provider id string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential replaces the deleted PROVIDER_ID constant, creating hand-maintained duplicate that would break on rename

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which looks up the provider via a hardcoded string: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. In the same PR, `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction` removes usage/import of `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` and now calls this helper instead. This creates a duplicated, hand-maintained provider ID that could drift if the provider ID is renamed, but nothing in the diff proves an immediate runtime failure (the string may be correct today).

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateCredential sends raw plain-text JSON codes as challengeResponse to arbitrary CredentialInputUpdater implementations via an undocumented wire contract

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the code serializes the newly generated recovery codes into a plain-text JSON string (`JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`) and wraps it in a `UserCredentialModel` passed to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. For user-storage-backed users, this routes that JSON through the `CredentialInput` interface (effectively via `getChallengeResponse()`), i.e., an implicit/undocumented contract for `CredentialInputUpdater` implementations that support `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`. The diff even updates a user storage provider (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`) to store `input.getChallengeResponse()` as credential data, confirming the contract. This is a real API/design concern (and potentially a security consideration), but the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s a correctness/security defect in Keycloak itself—providers can choose how to store/handle it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes") result used without null check, causing NPE when feature is disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` the result of `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")` is used without a null check (`recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)`). The diff does not show any guarantee in this method that the provider is always registered, so this is a real edge-case robustness issue. However, the finding’s specific claim that it will happen “when feature is disabled” is not verifiable from the diff alone (the call path may be gated elsewhere by feature checks).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes stored as plaintext in user storage in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential, violating hashed-at-rest invariant

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, when attempting to store recovery codes in a federated user storage, the code serializes `generatedCodes` (the raw recovery codes) to JSON (`JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`) and then stores it via `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson))`. That `challengeResponse` is then persisted by the user storage implementation as credential data (e.g., in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential(...)` it does `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`), meaning the recovery codes are stored in plaintext-at-rest in user storage. This is a concrete security defect introduced/exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test asserts recovery code storage format; assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage only checks a boolean and passes for plaintext storage

adjudication.rationale: The newly added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` only asserts presence via `assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage(true)`, which in turn calls `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageFactory.hasRecoveryCodes()` and checks only `user.getRecoveryCodes() != null` (boolean existence). It does not validate the actual stored representation (e.g., that `createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` stored a JSON-serialized `List<String>` in `UserCredentialModel` challenge response / `CredentialModel.credentialData`). So the test would still pass even if the storage format were incorrect (including plaintext vs other encodings), making this a specific coverage gap tied to the new recovery-code storage logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single-use semantics for recovery codes dropped on user-storage path; codes are never marked as used and remain valid forever

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a user-storage (federated) path for recovery codes: `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` first calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` with JSON-serialized codes in `challengeResponse`, and only falls back to local storage if that returns false. In the provided federated storage implementation (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`), recovery codes validation (`isValid` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`) only deserializes the stored list and checks `anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, with no removal/rotation/update of the used code. This makes recovery codes reusable on the user-storage path (not single-use), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies replay protection (second login with used code is never asserted)

adjudication.rationale: The new test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest` performs only a single login using one generated recovery code (`enterRecoveryCodes(...); clickSignInButton();`) and never attempts a second authentication reusing the same code to assert it is rejected/invalidated. Given this PR adds recovery-code support in user storage (`CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, and storage provider handling), a replay-protection assertion would be a specific missing test for this newly exercised flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: credentialModelOpt.get() in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean throws NoSuchElementException when user has no recovery-code credential, producing a 500 instead of a proper challenge/failure

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the constructor now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking `isPresent()`. If the user has no recovery-codes credential (neither federated nor local), this will throw `NoSuchElementException`, which would typically result in an unhandled server error rather than a controlled flow outcome.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IOException in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials logs and silently drops the recovery-codes credential, locking the user out with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)`, the new recovery-codes branch catches `IOException` from `JsonSerialization.readValue(...)`, logs `log.error("Could not deserialize  credential of type: recovery-codes")`, and then simply does not add the recovery-codes credential to the returned stream. That part of the finding (“logs and silently drops”) is accurate in the diff. However, the stronger claim that this definitively “locks the user out with no error surfaced” is not directly verifiable from the diff, because (a) normal data written by this same diff uses `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` so `IOException` should be rare, and (b) login validation in this provider uses `myUser.recoveryCodes` directly in `isValid(...)`, not `getCredentials(...)`. The concern is still real for corrupted/legacy data because callers like `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` depend on federated credentials streams and could observe the credential as missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single-use invalidation of recovery codes in user storage is not implemented or tested — the consumption path never removes a used code, so code reuse is not verified or prevented

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added user-storage support for recovery codes, validation does not consume/invalidate a used code. In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the recovery-codes branch only deserializes the stored list and checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, with no update/removal of the matched code from `myUser.recoveryCodes`. The new test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only logs in once with a recovery code and does not attempt reuse, so reuse prevention is neither implemented nor verified for the user-storage path introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: User-storage credential written by CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential carries raw plaintext recovery codes while local storage stores the hashed model, creating inconsistent security postures for the same credential type

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the federated/user-storage path serializes `generatedCodes` and writes them via `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)` then `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. In the added backwards-compat user storage provider, `updateCredential` persists `input.getChallengeResponse()` into `CredentialModel.setCredentialData(...)`, and `isValid` later deserializes that JSON and compares the input code directly (`anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`). This shows the user-storage implementation will persist and validate raw plaintext recovery codes, which is a real security defect for a credential type (and differs from the local-storage path which stores a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` instead of the raw list).

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean refactor to Optional is cosmetic — it calls get() with no presence check, and the new getCredential fall-through can make the Optional empty for federated users, causing NoSuchElementException/HTTP 500 instead of a 4xx re-challenge

adjudication.rationale: The bean still dereferences without a presence check, but it already did so before (previously: `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst().get()`). The new `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` explicitly *adds* a federated-first lookup with a fallback to stored credentials via `.or(() -> ...stored...)`, so it does not create a new “Optional empty for federated users” scenario grounded in this diff. Any potential `NoSuchElementException` if no credential exists is pre-existing and not newly introduced by the Optional refactor shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage test fixture, whose documented invariant is that it stays unmodified across Keycloak versions, was changed with ~70 lines of recovery-code handling, destroying the backwards-compat invariant the test suite exists to enforce

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify the BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage test provider substantially to add recovery-code support (e.g., supportsCredentialType now includes RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE; updateCredential stores recovery codes; new getCredentials() implementation; new validation branch; MyUser gains recoveryCodes; factory gains hasRecoveryCodes). This directly conflicts with the file’s own stated intent/comments that it is a provider “created in Keycloak 4.8.3” and that “Future Keycloak versions should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider,” i.e., a backwards-compat fixture. While not a runtime defect, it is a scope/test-architecture concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reformat-only rewrite of getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory in CredentialHelper adds unrelated whitespace churn that inflates the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows only indentation/whitespace changes to `getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory` in `CredentialHelper` (leading spaces adjusted, no logic change). Calling this out as “whitespace churn” is a pure formatting/style nit rather than a defect or substantive review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes takes a delay parameter and wires a 'delayed-authenticator' execution, but the only caller passes 0 — dead speculative generality

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes(KeycloakTestingClient testingClient, long delay)` is only called with `0` in `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()`, so the parameter currently isn’t used for variability. However, this is at most a minor test-helper generality/cleanup nit, not a verifiable defect or a substantive review issue impacting behavior introduced by the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Provider id hardcoded as string literal 'keycloak-recovery-authn-codes' in CredentialHelper instead of referencing RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID, creating two spellings of the provider id that can silently drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which obtains the provider via `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`, hardcoding the provider id string literal. Elsewhere in the codebase (and previously in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction`, whose `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` import/usage was removed in this diff) the provider id is typically referenced via the factory constant. This introduces duplicate spellings of the id that could drift if the constant changes, creating a maintainability/consistency risk, though not an immediate functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: userStorage write path stores raw recovery codes while local path stores hashed codes, creating two divergent on-disk formats with no SPI contract defining which is canonical, causing deserialization errors for federated providers

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the user-storage (federated) write path stores a JSON string of `generatedCodes` (raw codes) via `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)` and `updateCredential(...)`. However, the claim that the local-storage path “stores hashed codes” is not verifiable from this diff: the local path calls `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` but the provider’s implementation/format is not shown here. Also, the diff does not show any SPI contract issue or concrete deserialization failure scenario across formats—only the test provider explicitly serializes/deserializes JSON lists for its own storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Regenerating recovery codes for a federated user leaves a stale local credential of the same type in place with no invalidation, so a rotated credential remains valid at login

adjudication.rationale: The new `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` first attempts `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` (federated/user-storage) and, if that succeeds, it does not remove/disable any existing local stored credential of the same type; it only falls back to creating a local credential when user-storage update returns false. This can leave both a federated and a local `recovery-codes` credential present after regeneration/rotation. The diff shows no invalidation/deletion of the local one in the success path, so stale local recovery-code data can remain in place and potentially still be accepted depending on credential validation selection/iteration order.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated isValid path compares recovery codes and returns true without marking them consumed, so single-use codes work an unlimited number of times

adjudication.rationale: In the federated user storage implementation `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the newly added recovery-codes branch validates by deserializing the stored JSON list and returning `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without removing/marking the matched code as consumed or persisting any update. This means a recovery code can be reused indefinitely when stored in federated storage, contradicting the expected single-use behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Optional-returning helper RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential's only new caller calls .get() unconditionally, causing raw NoSuchElementException (HTTP 500) in bean construction when no credential exists

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the new code calls `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` and then immediately does `credentialModelOpt.get()` with no presence check. Since `getCredential()` can return `Optional.empty()` when neither federated nor local recovery-codes credentials exist, this will throw `NoSuchElementException` during bean construction (likely resulting in a 500). Other new usage (`RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`) checks `isPresent()`, but this bean does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test config alias typo 'delayed-suthenticator-config' in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:133

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `config.setAlias("delayed-suthenticator-config")` inside `configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes(...)`, but this alias is just a free-form label for the execution config and is not referenced anywhere else in the shown changes. A misspelling in an unused alias string is not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes stored as plaintext instead of SHA-512 hashes for federated users, dropping the security contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which, for federated/user-storage, serializes `generatedCodes` (the human-readable recovery codes) to JSON and stores them via `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson))`. In the backwards-compat user storage provider, `updateCredential` persists this JSON directly into `CredentialModel.credentialData` and `isValid` deserializes it and compares the stored values directly against the user-entered `input.getChallengeResponse()`. There is no hashing step in this federated path, so recovery codes are stored/validated as plaintext for federated users, unlike the local-storage path which uses `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` (likely handling proper encoding/hashing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two incompatible on-disk formats for the same credential type, diverging between local and federated paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff creates RecoveryAuthnCodes credentials via two different persistence paths with different serialized payloads: in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` the federated/user-storage path calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson))`, where `challengeResponse` is a JSON array of *raw* codes (`JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`). If that returns false, the local-storage path instead calls `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` using a `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` (whose internal storage format is not shown here and may differ, e.g., include structured/hashed fields). This demonstrates divergent storage representations for the same credential type between federated vs local, creating a compatibility/contract concern for providers consuming `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` vs stored credentials. The diff does not conclusively show runtime breakage, but it does show format divergence being introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credential lookup order changed from local-only to federated-first, orphaning/shadowing existing local credentials without a migration or precedence rule

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change recovery-code credential lookup from local-only to federated-first: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` filters `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` first and only falls back to `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream()`. Call sites were updated accordingly (e.g., `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`, `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`). Additionally, `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential()` may create/update a federated credential via `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` but does not remove any existing local stored credential of the same type, so a user could end up with both; in that case federated will shadow local. However, the diff doesn’t demonstrate that this is definitively incorrect behavior (it may be intended to prefer user storage), so this is a legitimate edge-case/precedence/migration concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage modified, destroying its purpose of testing unmodified legacy providers; a separate provider should have been created

adjudication.rationale: The diff directly modifies the testsuite legacy provider `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` to add Recovery Codes support (e.g., `supportsCredentialType` now accepts `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, `updateCredential` persists recovery codes, and a new `getCredentials` override exposes them). This provider is explicitly described as a Keycloak 4.8.3-era implementation for backwards compatibility testing, so changing it undermines the goal of testing newer Keycloak versions against an *unmodified* legacy provider. This is a scope/testing-architecture concern rather than a runtime defect in production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded provider id string 'keycloak-recovery-authn-codes' replaces the PROVIDER_ID constant, risking silent null and NPE if the id changes

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the provider is looked up with a hardcoded string: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. The diff also shows `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction` stopped using `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` and now calls this helper. While the string may currently match the provider id, hardcoding it creates a maintenance risk: if the provider id changes, `getProvider(...)` could return null and the later `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` call (no null-check) would NPE. The diff alone does not prove the id is wrong today, so it’s not a verifiable immediate defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error semantics changed to a bare RuntimeException with no message, thrown after codes are displayed but before persistence, leaving the required action pending and codes invalid

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, which serializes `generatedCodes` via `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` and, on `IOException`, throws `new RuntimeException(e)` with no custom message (and without any fallback persistence path). This exception is thrown before either `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` (user storage) or `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` (local DB) can run, so a failure here would abort the required-action POST and leave the credential unpersisted (thus the action still pending and the user holding codes that were not saved).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plaintext recovery codes handed to user-storage providers via updateCredential and stored/compared unhashed, defeating 2FA for federated users

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly serializes the *raw* generated recovery codes to JSON and passes them as the `challengeResponse` to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`. In the federated user-storage implementation shown (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`), that `challengeResponse` is stored directly as `CredentialModel.credentialData` (no hashing), and `isValid(...)` later deserializes it and compares with `equals(input.getChallengeResponse())`, i.e., plaintext comparison. This demonstrates federated recovery codes can be stored and verified unhashed via the updateCredential path introduced/used here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery codes in user-storage path are replayable: no single-use consumption, isValid never marks codes as used

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds recovery-codes support to the federated user storage implementation (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`). In `isValid(...)`, the recovery-codes branch deserializes the stored JSON list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, but it never removes the matched code or updates persisted state to mark it consumed. This makes recovery codes replayable in the user-storage path, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean constructor calls Optional.get() without presence check, causing NoSuchElementException/500 error on login page

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the constructor now calls `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` and then immediately does `credentialModelOpt.get()` with no `isPresent()`/`orElseThrow` guard. If the user has no recovery-codes credential in either federated or local storage, this will throw `NoSuchElementException`, which can surface as a 500 while rendering the page. This unsafe `Optional.get()` usage is visible directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The else branch of createRecoveryCodesCredential (local-storage fallback via recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential) is never exercised by any test in the diff; only the user-storage-created branch is tested

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the fallback `else` branch calls `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` returns false. The added test `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` explicitly asserts the recovery codes are stored in the user storage (`assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage(true)`), which corresponds to the `userStorageCreated == true` path. No test in the diff sets up a scenario where `updateCredential(...)` returns false (e.g., a user storage that doesn't support recovery codes), so the local-storage fallback branch is not exercised by tests shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The IOException to RuntimeException branch in createRecoveryCodesCredential is unreachable dead code since JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString on a List<String> won't throw, and the RuntimeException wrap has no error context

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` is inside a `try`/`catch (IOException e)`. From the diff, this call is a general JSON serialization utility (likely Jackson-based) whose signature can throw `IOException`/`JsonProcessingException` even when serializing a `List<String>`, so the catch branch is not verifiably unreachable dead code based on the diff alone. The critique about missing error context is subjective, but the core claim (unreachable dead code) misreads what can be concluded from the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The test adds a delayed-authenticator execution with delay=0 that is dead scaffolding — nothing tests or depends on the delay, adding an untested moving part to the flow under test

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes(...)` the test flow always adds a required `"delayed-authenticator"` execution and configures it with `delay` (and the test calls it with `delay=0`). In `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` there is no assertion about timing or any behavior that would differ based on `delay`, so this adds an extra required authenticator (an additional moving part / dependency in the flow) without the test actually exercising the delay behavior it introduces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The test never verifies recovery code consumption/invalidation — no assertion that a used code fails on second login or that getCredential's federated-first lookup returns updated credentials, so code replay regressions would pass

adjudication.rationale: The newly added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only performs a single login using one recovery code (`enterRecoveryCodes(...); clickSignInButton();`) and never attempts a second login reusing the same code to assert consumption/invalidation semantics. Likewise, the diff introduces `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` with a federated-first lookup, but no test asserts behavior when credentials are consumed/updated (e.g., that the fetched credential reflects post-use state or that replay fails). This is a concrete coverage gap for the newly added recovery-codes federated-storage logic rather than a directly verifiable functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The enterRecoveryCodes helper conflates 1-based code numbers with 0-based list indices — passing an int directly as a list index risks an off-by-one entering the wrong recovery code, masking a potential numbering bug

adjudication.rationale: In the added test helper `enterRecoveryCodes(...)`, the index used is `generatedRecoveryAuthnCodes.get(requestedCode)`, where `requestedCode` comes from `EnterRecoveryAuthnCodePage#getRecoveryAuthnCodeToEnterNumber()`. The diff does not show whether that number is 0-based or 1-based, so an off-by-one defect cannot be verified from the PR. Additionally, the only call site in the diff passes `expectedCode` as `0` and asserts `requestedCode == expectedCode`, suggesting the test expects 0-based numbering, making the direct list indexing consistent with the test’s own expectation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: createRecoveryCodesCredential discards the hashed credentialModel and writes unhashed recovery codes in an incompatible format (bare JSON array) for user-storage users, causing parsing failures and lockout when the credential is read back

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the user-storage path (`user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` returning true) ignores the provided `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel credentialModel` and instead serializes `generatedCodes` to a plain JSON array string (`JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`) and stores it via `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`. The local-storage path, by contrast, persists `credentialModel` via `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)`. This creates an inconsistent persistence format and (at least) stores raw recovery codes for federated/user-storage users rather than whatever encoded/hashed representation `credentialModel` encapsulates, which is a correctness/security regression implied by the differing code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cleanup of pre-existing local recovery-codes credential when regeneration lands in user storage, leaving a stale shadow credential that can silently reactivate if the federation is removed

adjudication.rationale: The new flow can leave an existing local (KC DB) recovery-codes credential in place when regeneration succeeds in federated user storage. In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, if `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` returns true (meaning the federated/user-storage path handled it), the code only logs and does not remove any previously stored local credential. Meanwhile `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` explicitly falls back to `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)` when federated credentials are absent, so a stale local credential would become effective again if federation is removed/disabled. The diff shows no cleanup/removal of the local shadow credential in this successful user-storage branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getCredential precedence change silently shadows an existing local recovery-codes credential with any federated credential of the same type, with no backfill or reconciliation before the read path switches

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` which searches federated credentials first (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()...findFirst()`) and only then falls back to local stored credentials (`or(() -> ...getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst())`). Call sites in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` and `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` were changed from local-only reads to this new method, so if both a federated and a local recovery-codes credential exist, the federated one will be used and the local one effectively ignored. The diff does not include any reconciliation/backfill logic for that dual-presence case. However, the diff also adds `createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` that attempts to create/update in user storage first and only creates locally if that fails, suggesting the precedence may be intentional; the problematic dual-presence scenario is not shown as being created by this PR itself (it would rely on existing data/state).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test provider updateCredential overwrites the recovery-codes field without round-trip of consumed-code state, and isValid compares against the full stored list without removing used codes, so codes are never marked used

adjudication.rationale: In the added federation test provider `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`, recovery codes are stored as a JSON list in `updateCredential(...)` (`recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`) and `isValid(...)` simply deserializes that list and checks `anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`. There is no logic anywhere in this diff to remove or mark a code as consumed after successful validation, nor to persist an updated list back to storage. As a result, recovery codes in this user storage provider can be reused indefinitely, which violates expected one-time recovery-code semantics and makes the provider behavior incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated user credentialData stored as raw JSON array of code strings causes RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel to throw a parsing exception (500 error) during login validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff does store the generated recovery codes as a JSON array string when calling `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` (in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`). However, the only concrete federated/user-storage implementation shown (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`) does not expose that raw JSON array to login parsing: it overrides `getCredentials(...)` and *deserializes* `credentialData` and then constructs a proper `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`. Additionally, the login-side code now fetches the credential via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)`, but the diff does not show `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(...)` failing on a JSON array nor any thrown parsing exception path tied to this change. Therefore the claimed 500 due to JSON-array parsing is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: credentialModelOpt.get() is called without an isPresent() guard in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean, causing NoSuchElementException and a 500 error when no recovery-codes credential exists

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the diff changes credential lookup to `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` but then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` when creating `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`. There is no `isPresent()`/`orElseThrow()` guard, so if the user has no recovery-codes credential (and `getCredential()` returns `Optional.empty()`), this will throw `NoSuchElementException`, plausibly resulting in a 500 during page rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials silently swallows IOException and omits the recovery-codes credential from the returned stream, causing inconsistency with isConfiguredFor

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(), if JsonSerialization.readValue(...) throws IOException, the catch block only logs `log.error("Could not deserialize  credential of type: recovery-codes")` and does not add any recovery-codes credential to `credentialModels`, so the returned stream omits it. Meanwhile isConfiguredFor() reports the user configured for recovery codes solely based on `myUser.recoveryCodes != null`. This creates a verifiable inconsistency between configuration state and enumerated credentials when deserialization fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single-use semantics are lost for user-storage users: no code consumes/marks a used recovery code in the federated path, allowing indefinite replay of the same recovery code

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces storing recovery codes in federated/user-storage via `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` by calling `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson))` when user storage supports it. In the federated test provider (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`), `isValid(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` merely deserializes the stored JSON list and checks `anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without removing/marking the matched code as used or updating the stored credential. No other code in the diff updates the federated credential after successful use. This allows the same recovery code to be replayed indefinitely for user-storage users, breaking expected single-use semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes") result is never null-checked before calling .createCredential, causing NPE when the RECOVERY_CODES feature is disabled; also the provider id constant was replaced with duplicated hand-typed string literals

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the code does `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")` and then unconditionally calls `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` without a null-check, so it is not defensive if the provider is unavailable. The diff also replaces use of `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` (removed in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction`) with a hand-typed string literal, which is a maintainability/consistency issue. However, the claim that this definitively causes an NPE specifically "when the RECOVERY_CODES feature is disabled" is not verifiable from the diff alone (feature gating / provider availability behavior isn’t shown), and the string literal is not shown duplicated in multiple places in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: users.get(translateUserName(user.getUsername())) in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential dereferences the map result without a null check, causing NPE for users absent from the map instead of the local-storage fallback

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential(...)`, the diff shows direct dereference of `users.get(translateUserName(user.getUsername()))` when assigning credentials (e.g., `... .otp = newOTP;` and newly added `... .recoveryCodes = recoveryCodesModel;`) with no null check. If the username is not present in the `users` map, `users.get(...)` returns null and the assignment will throw an NPE. The finding’s “local-storage fallback” phrasing isn’t shown in this diff, but the NPE risk from the unchecked map lookup is verifiable from the code.
